{"id":"01a106b8-0433-7ad0-8fb8-75dc59e7f68d","type":"hazard","summary":"Database connections in deployed environments","content":"In production and staging the app never connects to Postgres directly; every connection goes through a pooler on port 6432 that the platform team manages. Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. The pooler runs in transaction mode: session state does not survive between transactions (no SET session variables, no advisory locks across transactions, no LISTEN/NOTIFY), and server-side prepared statements fail with 'prepared statement does not exist'. With psycopg 3 you must connect with `prepare_threshold=None` to turn automatic prepared statements off.","physical":["src/","docker-compose.yml"],"logical":["database"],"tags":["database","postgres"],"criticality":0.7,"confidence":0.8,"status":"active","visibility":"shared","provenance":"human","epistemic":"fact"}

Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. The pooler runs in transaction mode: session state does not survive between transactions (no SET session variables, no advisory locks across transactions, no LISTEN/NOTIFY), and server-side prepared statements fail with 'prepared statement does not exist'. With psycopg 3 you must connect with `prepare_threshold=None` to turn automatic prepared statements off.

```python
def get_conn():
    return psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"], prepare_threshold=None)
```

- **`prepare_threshold=None` is on purpose.** A project memory says production and staging reach Postgres through a pooler on port 6432 that only holds a connection for one transaction at a time. psycopg's automatic prepared statements break there with "prepared statement does not exist". You won't see that locally, because docker-compose connects straight to Postgres on 5432.
- **It fails fast if `DATABASE_URL` isn't set**, raising a `KeyError` instead of quietly connecting to some default database.
- **Use it as a context manager**, e.g. `with get_conn() as conn:`. Keep transactions short: each service only gets 20 pooled connections, and long transactions starve checkout.

I only checked that the file compiles; I didn't open a real connection.
